Because the pressure differential holds the vibration device 10 against the covering element 36 while the bearing face 26 is of a low-friction material, the vibration device 10 is held down and at the same time free to move over the exposed face 38, unlike a device that is gripped at one place. The vibration produced by the vibration motor 18 acts through the stirring elements 48 to produce a constant forward motion of the vibration device 10 over the exposed face 38. The vibration device 10 therefore advances from area to area of the covering element 36 without tension being applied to a flexible pulling element 46 and without being guided by hand, while the pressure differential is maintained throughout. The hold is not loosened to permit that motion: the air-extraction mechanism 20 continues to run and the pressure differential continues to press the bearing face 26 onto the exposed face 38 while the vibration device 10 advances, so the vibration coupling into the covering element 36 is not interrupted by the movement. The stirring elements 48 are shown schematically in FIG. 6.
